network_state: NETWORK ENABLED. github.com API and private Git HTTPS access, Supabase, Vercel, Twilio, and npm registry endpoints produced live responses. GitHub’s deliberate invalid-token call returned an authentication-specific HTTP 401, confirming failures are observable. gcloud is not network-blocked; its snap confinement/DBus launcher failure occurs before the network probe can run.
mcp_readiness: Codex-side MCP readiness is currently absent: `~/.codex/config.toml` has no `mcp_servers` or profiles sections, and `codex mcp list` confirms zero servers. A usable per-profile allowlist would need named profiles, explicitly configured MCP server commands/endpoints, credential injection through approved environment/keychain mechanisms, and a least-privilege tool allowlist emphasizing read operations such as PR/repository metadata, CI/log reads, Supabase schema inspection, and cloud service/log listing. Write, deploy, migration/DDL, secret-management, and destructive tools should be omitted or approval-gated per profile.
seat_readiness_verdict: PARTIALLY READY TODAY. A Codex seat can perform genuine read-heavy GitHub PR/repository review, private Git reads, Supabase project discovery, and Vercel project discovery. Concrete blockers: gcloud is unusable because the snap cannot create its transient scope, preventing Cloud Run/log access; no MCP servers or profiles exist, so there is no connector-based read surface; Twilio’s configured Standard API Key could not authenticate to the chosen account-read endpoint; npm is unauthenticated; and database/schema inspection was intentionally not attempted because it would require reading environment credentials. Codex itself, GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, and private-origin Git transport are authenticated.
